name: github
description: Read and open issues, comments and pull requests in GitHub repositories, signed in with your own GitHub App.

tools.name: list_repositories
tools.description: List the repositories the agent's access names, with whether each is private and when it last changed. Reads only.

tools.name: get_repository
tools.description: Read a repository's details: description, default branch, visibility, address. Reads only.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: List a repository's issues by state, labels or search words, at most 50. Reads only.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: Read one issue with its body and latest 20 comments. Reads only.

tools.name: create_issue
tools.description: Open an issue in a repository, when the agent's access allows creating and commenting. Creates an issue as the account you signed in with.

tools.name: comment
tools.description: Comment on an issue or pull request, when the agent's access allows creating and commenting. Posts a comment as the account you signed in with.

tools.name: list_pull_requests
tools.description: List a repository's pull requests by state or base branch, at most 50. Reads only.

tools.name: get_pull_request
tools.description: Read one pull request, and its diff when asked. Reads only.

tools.name: create_pull_request
tools.description: Open a pull request from a branch already on GitHub, when the agent's access allows creating and commenting. Creates a pull request as the account you signed in with; moves no commits.

tools.name: list_branches
tools.description: List a repository's branches and the commit each points at. Reads only.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Compare two branches, tags or commits: commits ahead and behind, files changed. Reads only.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Name the GitHub account the connection signs in as, for Test connection. Reads only.

repositories.title: Repositories
repositories.description: Each one owner/name, such as acme/widgets, or a pattern such as acme/*, which covers every repository directly under acme. * is the only wildcard. Capitals do not matter.

write.title: May create and comment
write.description: Lets the agent open issues and pull requests and comment on them in those repositories, as the account you signed in with.

kivali.setup_notes:
Agents reach GitHub through a GitHub App you register yourself, once. Register it on the account that owns the repositories agents should reach: the app can reach only that account's repositories.

[Register the app on your personal account](https://github.com/settings/apps/new?description=Lets%20Kivali%20agents%20work%20with%20issues%20and%20pull%20requests.&url=https%3A%2F%2Fkivali.ai&callback_urls%5B%5D={{redirect_url}}&callback_urls%5B%5D=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%2Fconnect%2Fcallback&callback_urls%5B%5D={{external_redirect_url}}&request_oauth_on_install=false&public=false&webhook_active=false&contents=read&issues=write&metadata=read&pull_requests=write)

Using an organization? Copy this address, put the organization's name in place of `ORGANIZATION`, and open it in your browser:

```Organization address
https://github.com/organizations/ORGANIZATION/settings/apps/new?description=Lets%20Kivali%20agents%20work%20with%20issues%20and%20pull%20requests.&url=https%3A%2F%2Fkivali.ai&callback_urls%5B%5D={{redirect_url}}&callback_urls%5B%5D=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%2Fconnect%2Fcallback&callback_urls%5B%5D={{external_redirect_url}}&request_oauth_on_install=false&public=false&webhook_active=false&contents=read&issues=write&metadata=read&pull_requests=write
```

GitHub's form opens with Kivali's settings filled in: this team's callback URLs, the permissions agents need, no webhook, and installation only on that account. Then:

1. Give the app a name. GitHub App names are unique across GitHub.
2. Tick **Enable Device Flow**, and leave everything else as it is.
3. Choose **Create GitHub App**.
4. Copy the **Client ID** into **Client id** below. Choose **Generate a new client secret** and paste it into **Client secret** below. GitHub shows it once.
5. Choose **Install App**, install the app on the account, and choose the repositories agents should reach. Agents reach only repositories the app is installed on, and only those their access names.

Then choose **Save connection**, and **Sign in**.

If you later give this team an address for other computers (**Other devices** in Kivali Desktop), or change it, add that address followed by `/connect/callback` to the app's callback URLs on GitHub.
